tracks.name: Data Science
tracks.focus: Counting, ranking, streaming statistics, sampling and sequence similarity, what data interviews actually probe.

tracks.name: AI Engineer
tracks.focus: Caches (KV / prompt), tries and prefix search, tokenisation-style DP, schedulers and streaming, the plumbing under LLM apps.

tracks.name: Forward Deployed Engineer
tracks.focus: Messy-data wrangling, parsers, rate limits, integrations and graph joins, the problems you hit at a customer site.

tracks.name: AI/ML Researcher
tracks.focus: Numerics, sampling, dynamic programming and graph optimisation, the algorithmic ideas behind ML research code.

tracks.name: Software Engineer
tracks.focus: The classic generalist loop: arrays, strings, lists, trees, graphs, DP and backtracking at medium difficulty.

tracks.name: Backend Engineer
tracks.focus: Caches, rate limiters, schedulers, dependency graphs and data-structure design, server-side building blocks.

tracks.name: Frontend Engineer
tracks.focus: Debounce, throttle, memoize, event emitters and promise utilities in JavaScript, plus the DOM-flavoured DSA you get asked.

tracks.name: Core Developer
tracks.focus: Systems-level fundamentals: bit tricks, string matching, interpreters, memory-style structures and careful recursion.

two-sum.br: Return the indices of the two numbers that add up to target.
two-sum.trick: "Looking for a pair?" → ask "have I seen the complement?" Store what you have passed, query what you need.
two-sum.real: Join keys in feature stores and de-duplicating records by a derived key.

longest-substring-without-repeating-char.br: Length of the longest substring in which every character is unique.
longest-substring-without-repeating-char.trick: "Longest window with a rule" → grow right, and when the rule breaks shrink left. Each character enters and leaves once.
longest-substring-without-repeating-char.real: Streaming dedup windows; longest unique run in a token stream.

median-of-two-sorted-arrays.br: Median of two sorted arrays in O(log(min(m,n))).
median-of-two-sorted-arrays.trick: Don’t merge. Binary-search how many elements of the shorter array sit in the left half; the rest is forced. A cut is right when each left border ≤ the opposite right border.
median-of-two-sorted-arrays.real: Order statistics across sharded sorted data, percentiles from several sorted partitions.

regular-expression-matching.br: Does the pattern (with . and *) match the entire string?
regular-expression-matching.trick: dp[i][j] = "first i chars of s match first j chars of p". A "*" either vanishes (look two columns left) or eats one more char (look one row up).
regular-expression-matching.real: How regex engines work; the same table-based thinking underlies glob matching and tokenizers.

container-with-most-water.pat: Two Pointers (shrink from the shorter wall)
container-with-most-water.br: Pick two vertical lines that hold the most water.
container-with-most-water.trick: "Widest first" → start at both ends and always throw away the SHORTER wall; the taller one may still pair with something better.
container-with-most-water.real: Any two-ended greedy search where width trades off against quality.

longest-common-prefix.br: Longest starting string shared by every word.
longest-common-prefix.trick: "Common prefix of many" → only compare the alphabetically smallest and largest; everything else sits between them.
longest-common-prefix.real: Prefix caching: sharing the common prefix of prompts lets an LLM server reuse its KV cache.

3sum.br: All unique triplets that sum to zero.
3sum.trick: "k-Sum" → sort, fix one number, then Two-Sum-II with two pointers on the rest. Skip equal neighbours to avoid duplicates.
3sum.real: Finding balancing combinations in sorted score/cost lists.

valid-parentheses.br: Are all brackets closed in the right order?
valid-parentheses.trick: "Nested / balanced" → last opened, first closed = a stack. Push openers, pop on closers.
valid-parentheses.real: HTML/JSON/JSX parsing and validating nested tags in the DOM.

merge-two-sorted-lists.br: Merge two sorted linked lists into one sorted list.
merge-two-sorted-lists.trick: "Merge sorted things" → two fingers, always take the smaller head. A dummy node saves the edge case.
merge-two-sorted-lists.real: Merge step of merge sort and of sorted-shard compaction.

generate-parentheses.br: All well-formed strings with n pairs of parentheses.
generate-parentheses.trick: "Valid by construction" → never build an invalid prefix: add "(" if you have some left, add ")" only if closers < openers.
generate-parentheses.real: Grammar-constrained generation: only emit tokens that keep the output valid.

merge-k-sorted-lists.br: Merge k sorted linked lists into one sorted list.
merge-k-sorted-lists.trick: "Merge k sorted streams" → a min-heap holding ONE candidate per stream; pop the smallest, push that stream's next.
merge-k-sorted-lists.real: Merging beam-search candidates, k-way merge in LSM databases, merging sorted shards.

find-the-index-of-the-first-occurrence-i.t: Find the Index of the First Occurrence in a String
find-the-index-of-the-first-occurrence-i.br: Index of the first place needle appears in haystack (strStr).
find-the-index-of-the-first-occurrence-i.trick: "Don't re-read text" → on a mismatch fall back inside the NEEDLE using its own prefix-suffix table; the haystack pointer only goes forward.
find-the-index-of-the-first-occurrence-i.real: Streaming pattern matching in logs and parsers.

search-in-rotated-sorted-array.pat: Binary Search on the Sorted Half
search-in-rotated-sorted-array.br: A sorted array was rotated at an unknown pivot. Find target in O(log n).
search-in-rotated-sorted-array.trick: "Rotated array" → at least ONE half is always sorted. Check if target fits in that half; if not, go the other way.

combination-sum.br: All unique combinations that sum to target; each number may be reused.
combination-sum.trick: "All combinations" → at each level choose from index ≥ start so order cannot repeat; recurse, then undo (append / pop).

trapping-rain-water.br: How much rain water is trapped between the bars?
trapping-rain-water.trick: "Water on a bar" = min(tallest left, tallest right) − bar. Process the LOWER side first, its limit is already known.

group-anagrams.br: Group words that are anagrams of each other.
group-anagrams.trick: "Group by sameness" → invent a canonical key (sorted word or letter histogram) and let a dict do the grouping.
group-anagrams.real: Entity resolution: bucket records by a normalised signature before comparing.

powx-n.br: Compute x raised to the integer power n quickly.
powx-n.trick: Write the exponent in binary. Keep squaring x; multiply into the answer only for the 1-bits.
powx-n.real: Modular exponentiation in cryptography, matrix powers, fast Fibonacci.

n-queens.br: Place n queens on an n×n board so none attack each other.
n-queens.trick: "One queen per row" → recurse row by row; a square is safe if its column, its (r−c) diagonal and its (r+c) diagonal are free.
n-queens.real: Constraint satisfaction and pruning search, the idea behind SAT/CSP solvers.

maximum-subarray.br: Largest sum of any contiguous subarray.
maximum-subarray.trick: "Best contiguous sum" → at every element decide: extend the run or start fresh. Drop any negative baggage.
maximum-subarray.real: Finding the best contiguous window of gains, e.g. peak reward span in an RL episode.

merge-intervals.trick: "Overlapping ranges" → sort by start, then each interval either extends the last one or starts a new one.
merge-intervals.real: Merging time ranges: calendar free/busy, log windows, GPU reservation blocks.

text-justification.br: Pack words into lines of exactly maxWidth, spreading extra spaces evenly (left-heavy); the last line is left-justified.
text-justification.trick: Greedy-fill each line. Spaces per gap = divmod(extra spaces, gaps): everyone gets the quotient, the first "remainder" gaps get one more.
text-justification.real: Text layout engines, terminal formatters and PDF/typesetting line breaking.

sqrtx.br: Integer square root (round down) without using sqrt.
sqrtx.trick: "Largest value that still works" → binary search the ANSWER, not an array. Use mid = (lo+hi+1)//2 when you move lo = mid.
sqrtx.real: Newton / bisection root finding and numeric thresholds in loss functions.

climbing-stairs.br: Count the ways to climb n stairs taking 1 or 2 steps at a time.
climbing-stairs.trick: To stand on step n you came from n−1 or n−2 → ways(n) = ways(n−1) + ways(n−2). It is Fibonacci. Keep two variables.
climbing-stairs.real: Counting paths/compositions; the template for every "last step" recurrence.

simplify-path.br: Turn a Unix path into its canonical form.
simplify-path.trick: Split on "/". Skip empty and ".". ".." pops the stack. Everything else is pushed. Join with "/".
simplify-path.real: Path normalisation in file systems, web servers and static-site routers (and path-traversal defence).

edit-distance.br: Fewest insert/delete/replace operations to turn word1 into word2.
edit-distance.trick: Cell = cost to convert a prefix to a prefix. Same letter → copy the diagonal. Different → 1 + min(diagonal = replace, up = delete, left = insert).
edit-distance.real: Spell-check, fuzzy search, ASR word-error-rate, and string similarity metrics.

sort-colors.br: Sort an array of 0s, 1s and 2s in place.
sort-colors.trick: "Few distinct values" → partition into zones with 3 pointers: low / mid / high. One pass, in place.
sort-colors.real: Three-way partition inside quicksort; bucketing labels in place.

minimum-window-substring.br: Smallest substring of s that contains every character of t (with multiplicity).
minimum-window-substring.trick: "Smallest window that covers X" → expand right until covered, contract left until it breaks, record, repeat.
minimum-window-substring.real: Finding the shortest context span that contains all required evidence (retrieval snippets).

word-search.br: Is the word spelled by a path of adjacent cells (no cell reused)?
word-search.trick: "Path in a grid" → choose, explore, un-choose. Mark the cell visited in place and restore it on the way back.
word-search.real: Constraint search and puzzle solvers; the choose/explore/undo template.

largest-rectangle-in-histogram.br: Area of the largest rectangle that fits inside the bars.
largest-rectangle-in-histogram.trick: "Biggest rectangle" → every bar is the shortest of some rectangle. A shorter bar arriving tells the taller ones how far they stretched.
largest-rectangle-in-histogram.real: Largest contiguous region under a threshold, e.g. longest stretch of acceptable latency.

validate-binary-search-tree.br: Is the tree a valid binary search tree?
validate-binary-search-tree.trick: "BST check" → comparing to the parent is not enough. Carry an (lo, hi) window down: left child shrinks hi, right child raises lo.

binary-tree-level-order-traversal.br: Return node values level by level.
binary-tree-level-order-traversal.trick: "Level by level" → BFS with a queue; freeze len(queue) at the start of each round to know where the level ends.
binary-tree-level-order-traversal.real: Rendering trees breadth-first (DOM inspectors, org charts).

maximum-depth-of-binary-tree.br: Number of levels in a binary tree.
maximum-depth-of-binary-tree.trick: "Tree property" → trust recursion: answer(node) = 1 + max(answer(left), answer(right)), base case null = 0.
maximum-depth-of-binary-tree.real: Computing nesting depth of DOM / JSON / AST structures.

best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock.t: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock.br: Maximise profit from one buy followed by one later sell.
best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock.trick: "Best buy then sell" → at each day, assume you bought at the lowest price seen so far.
best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock.real: Max drawdown / max run-up on a metric time series.

valid-palindrome.br: Is the string a palindrome after ignoring case and non-alphanumerics?
valid-palindrome.trick: "Mirror check" → one finger at each end, walk toward the middle, skip junk.
valid-palindrome.real: Symmetry checks and two-ended scans in text normalisation.

longest-consecutive-sequence.br: Length of the longest run of consecutive integers (order in the array does not matter).
longest-consecutive-sequence.trick: "Consecutive without sorting" → only start counting at numbers whose predecessor is missing. Each run is walked once.
longest-consecutive-sequence.real: Detecting contiguous ID ranges, session gaps, missing sequence numbers.

clone-graph.trick: "Copy a graph" → one dictionary old→new. Check it before recursing: that stops infinite loops on cycles.
clone-graph.real: Deep-copying object graphs and compute graphs.

single-number.br: Every number appears twice except one, find it in O(1) space.
single-number.trick: a ^ a = 0 and a ^ 0 = a. XOR everything, duplicates annihilate.
single-number.real: Parity/checksum tricks; RAID parity and error detection use the same XOR cancellation.

copy-list-with-random-pointer.br: Deep-copy a list where each node also has a random pointer.
copy-list-with-random-pointer.trick: "Clone with extra pointers" → park each copy right after its original; then copy.random = original.random.next. No map needed.
copy-list-with-random-pointer.real: Deep-copying object graphs (config trees, ASTs) without a lookup table.

word-break.br: Can the string be split into dictionary words?
word-break.trick: dp[i] = "the first i letters can be built". It is true if some earlier True cell plus one dictionary word lands on i.
word-break.real: Tokenisation and word segmentation, the same idea as splitting text into vocabulary pieces.

linked-list-cycle.br: Does the linked list contain a cycle?
linked-list-cycle.trick: "Loop detection with no memory" → a slow and a fast runner. If there is a track loop, the fast one catches the slow one.
linked-list-cycle.real: Detecting cycles in dependency chains or pointer graphs.

lru-cache.br: A fixed-size cache that evicts the least recently used key. get/put should be O(1).
lru-cache.trick: Hash map for O(1) lookup + a linked list for O(1) "move to front / drop the back". OrderedDict is exactly that pair.
lru-cache.real: Every cache: CPU, CDN, DB buffer pool, and LLM prompt/KV-prefix caches.

evaluate-reverse-polish-notation.trick: "Postfix" → numbers go on the stack, an operator eats the top two and pushes the result. No parentheses ever needed.
evaluate-reverse-polish-notation.real: How compilers and calculators evaluate expressions; stack machines.

maximum-product-subarray.br: Largest product of any contiguous subarray (negatives can flip signs).
maximum-product-subarray.trick: "Product + negatives" → keep BOTH the biggest and smallest run; a minus sign turns the smallest into the biggest.
maximum-product-subarray.real: Compounded returns / multiplicative factors where sign flips matter.

min-stack.br: A stack that also returns its minimum in O(1).
min-stack.trick: "Extra query on a stack" → store the answer next to each item. When an item is popped, its snapshot goes with it.
min-stack.real: Running min/max with undo, e.g. monotonic stacks in editors and rollback.

find-peak-element.br: Find any index whose value is greater than both neighbours.
find-peak-element.trick: "Any peak" → follow the uphill side. If the right neighbour is bigger, a peak is guaranteed that way.
find-peak-element.real: Hill-climbing on a 1-D score such as picking the best learning-rate bucket.

reverse-bits.br: Reverse the bits of a 32-bit unsigned integer.
reverse-bits.trick: Swap halves, then quarters, then eighths… five swaps with masks reverse 32 bits.
reverse-bits.real: FFT bit-reversal permutation, endianness conversion, hardware bit tricks.

number-of-1-bits.br: Count the set bits (Hamming weight) of an integer.
number-of-1-bits.trick: n & (n−1) deletes the lowest 1-bit. Count how many deletions it takes to reach 0.
number-of-1-bits.real: Popcount: bitsets, Bloom filters, hashing, and compact feature flags.

house-robber.br: Maximise loot from a row of houses without robbing two neighbours.
house-robber.trick: At each house: skip (keep the best so far) or rob (this house + best from two back). Two rolling numbers are enough.
house-robber.real: Weighted interval choices with a no-adjacent constraint: scheduling jobs, non-overlapping ads.

number-of-islands.br: Count the groups of connected land cells in a grid.
number-of-islands.trick: "Count connected blobs" → scan; on unvisited land, count +1 and flood-fill the whole blob so it is never counted again.
number-of-islands.real: Connected-component labelling: image regions, clusters, contiguous free memory.

count-primes.br: How many primes are strictly less than n?
count-primes.trick: Do not test each number, let every prime cross out its multiples. Start at p² and stop at √n.

reverse-linked-list.trick: "Reverse in place" → three fingers: prev, cur, next. Save next, flip cur.next, slide everything one step.
reverse-linked-list.real: Undo stacks and reversing event chains without extra memory.

course-schedule.br: Can all courses be finished given prerequisite pairs? (Is the graph acyclic?)
course-schedule.trick: "Dependencies" → count unmet prerequisites per node; peel off nodes at 0. If you cannot peel everything, there is a cycle.
course-schedule.real: Build systems, ML pipeline DAGs, and autograd (backprop runs a topological order).

implement-trie-prefix-tree.br: insert, search and startsWith on a growing set of words.
implement-trie-prefix-tree.trick: "Prefix queries" → share common beginnings. Walk letter by letter; the cost is the length of the query, not the size of the dictionary.
implement-trie-prefix-tree.real: Autocomplete, tokenizer vocabularies and constrained decoding (only letters that keep a valid word).

course-schedule-ii.br: Return a valid order to take all courses, or [] if impossible.
course-schedule-ii.trick: Same peel-off-zero-in-degree loop as Course Schedule, just record the order you peel in.
course-schedule-ii.real: Dependency resolution in package managers and task orchestrators (Airflow-style DAG order).

design-add-and-search-words-data-structu.t: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure
design-add-and-search-words-data-structu.br: Words can be searched with '.' standing for any letter.
design-add-and-search-words-data-structu.trick: "Pattern with blanks" → trie for the letters, DFS that fans out only at a ".", everywhere else it follows one path.
design-add-and-search-words-data-structu.real: Wildcard routing and fuzzy matching of identifiers.

kth-largest-element-in-an-array.t: Kth Largest Element in an Array
kth-largest-element-in-an-array.br: The kth largest value in an unsorted array.
kth-largest-element-in-an-array.trick: "kth without sorting" → partition like quicksort but only follow ONE side. Average O(n). (Or keep a size-k min-heap.)
kth-largest-element-in-an-array.real: Top-k sampling over logits in LLM decoding, keep only the k best candidates.

contains-duplicate.br: Does any value appear at least twice?
contains-duplicate.trick: "Repeat?" → a set is a bouncer with a guest list: the second time someone shows up, stop.
contains-duplicate.real: Idempotency keys and duplicate-event filtering in pipelines.

invert-binary-tree.trick: "Mirror a tree" → at every node swap left and right. Order of visiting does not matter.
invert-binary-tree.real: Mirroring layouts (RTL UI) and symmetric tree transforms.

basic-calculator-ii.br: Evaluate an expression with + − * / and no parentheses.
basic-calculator-ii.trick: Remember the operator BEFORE each number. + / − push the number (signed); * / / combine it with the top of the stack immediately. Answer = sum(stack).
basic-calculator-ii.real: Expression parsers: spreadsheets, query-language WHERE clauses, config evaluators.

implement-queue-using-stacks.br: Build a FIFO queue using only stack operations.
implement-queue-using-stacks.trick: Reversing a stack twice restores order. Push into "in", and only when "out" runs dry pour "in" into it, every element moves at most once.
implement-queue-using-stacks.real: Amortised analysis made visible; the same trick builds queues in functional languages.

lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-tree.t: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree
lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-tree.br: The lowest node that has both p and q as descendants.
lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-tree.trick: "Meeting point" → ask each subtree "do you contain p or q?". The first node that hears YES from both sides is the answer.
lowest-common-ancestor-of-a-binary-tree.real: Finding the nearest shared parent in the DOM or in a dependency tree.

product-of-array-except-self.br: For each position, the product of all other numbers, without division.
product-of-array-except-self.trick: "Everything except me" = (stuff on my left) × (stuff on my right). Two sweeps, no division.

sliding-window-maximum.br: The maximum of every window of size k.
sliding-window-maximum.trick: "Max of a moving window" → a deque that stays sorted descending: pop weaker values from the back, expire old ones from the front.
sliding-window-maximum.real: Sliding-window attention masks and rolling max/min metrics.

valid-anagram.br: Are two strings made of exactly the same letters?
valid-anagram.trick: "Same letters?" → tally, don't sort. +1 for one word, −1 for the other, everything must cancel to zero.

meeting-rooms-ii.br: Minimum number of rooms so no meetings overlap in the same room.
meeting-rooms-ii.trick: "How many at once?" → keep a min-heap of end times; if the earliest end is before the next start, reuse that room.
meeting-rooms-ii.real: GPU / worker allocation: how many accelerators does a job queue need?

find-median-from-data-stream.br: Support addNum and findMedian on a growing stream.
find-median-from-data-stream.trick: "Running median" → split the data in two halves: a max-heap of the small half, a min-heap of the big half. The median sits at the roots.
find-median-from-data-stream.real: Streaming p50 latency and rolling quantiles in monitoring.

serialize-and-deserialize-binary-tree.br: Turn a tree into a string and rebuild the exact same tree.
serialize-and-deserialize-binary-tree.trick: "Round-trip a structure" → write it in preorder INCLUDING nulls; reading it back is the same recursion.
serialize-and-deserialize-binary-tree.real: Serialising trees / JSON-like structures for storage and RPC.

longest-increasing-subsequence.br: Length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.
longest-increasing-subsequence.trick: Keep, for each length, the smallest tail seen. A new number either extends the longest or replaces the first tail ≥ it.
longest-increasing-subsequence.real: Longest monotone trend; the core of diff/patience algorithms and sequence alignment.

burst-balloons.br: Choose the order of bursts to maximise coins; bursting i earns nums[i−1]·nums[i]·nums[i+1].
burst-balloons.trick: Think backwards: pick the LAST balloon k to burst in a gap. Its neighbours are then the fixed borders, and the two sides become independent.
burst-balloons.real: Interval DP: matrix-chain ordering, optimal BST, parsing, "choose the split point last".

coin-change.br: Fewest coins that make up an amount (or −1).
coin-change.trick: Build amounts from 0 upward: best(a) = 1 + min(best(a − coin)). Use amount+1 as "infinity".
coin-change.real: Minimum-cost decomposition: change-making, packet/chunk sizing, resource bundles.

longest-increasing-path-in-a-matrix.t: Longest Increasing Path in a Matrix
longest-increasing-path-in-a-matrix.br: Longest path of strictly increasing cells moving up/down/left/right.
longest-increasing-path-in-a-matrix.trick: "Strictly increasing" means the grid is a DAG, no cycles. So longest path from a cell is a fixed number: compute it once and cache it.
longest-increasing-path-in-a-matrix.real: Longest path in a DAG: build-dependency depth, critical-path analysis.

counting-bits.br: For every i in 0..n return its number of 1-bits.
counting-bits.trick: i is just (i >> 1) with one more bit on the end, so bits(i) = bits(i >> 1) + (i & 1).
counting-bits.real: Building popcount lookup tables; classic example of DP on binary structure.

top-k-frequent-elements.br: Return the k values that appear most often.
top-k-frequent-elements.trick: "Top-k by count" → counts are bounded by n, so use the count itself as an array index (bucket sort), no sorting needed.
top-k-frequent-elements.real: Most frequent tokens for vocabulary building; top queries in logs.

design-twitter.br: Post tweets, follow/unfollow, and fetch the 10 most recent tweets from you and your followees.
design-twitter.trick: Each user’s tweets are already time-ordered. The feed is "merge k sorted lists, stop after 10", a heap of each followee’s newest tweet.
design-twitter.real: Timeline fan-in for social feeds, activity streams and log aggregation.

design-hit-counter.br: Count hits in the last 300 seconds.
design-hit-counter.trick: Only 300 seconds matter, so keep 300 slots: second % 300. A slot with an older timestamp is stale and gets reused.
design-hit-counter.real: Rate limiters, request counters and "last 5 minutes" dashboards.

sum-of-two-integers.br: Add two integers without using + or −.
sum-of-two-integers.trick: XOR adds without carrying; (a & b) << 1 is the carry. Repeat until the carry dies. Mask to 32 bits in Python.
sum-of-two-integers.real: How an ALU adder works, half-adders chained into a full adder.

insert-delete-getrandom-o1.br: A set with O(1) insert, remove and uniformly random getRandom.
insert-delete-getrandom-o1.trick: Array = random access, dict = fast lookup. To delete from the middle in O(1): overwrite it with the last element and pop the end.
insert-delete-getrandom-o1.real: Random sampling from a dynamic pool: negative sampling, work stealing, A/B bucket picks.

shuffle-an-array.br: Return a uniformly random permutation, and support reset().
shuffle-an-array.trick: Walk from the back. For slot i pick a random j ≤ i and swap. Each of the n! orders has exactly the same chance.
shuffle-an-array.real: Shuffling datasets/minibatches for training, randomised experiments, card games.

decode-string.trick: "Nested brackets with counts" → on "[" save (text so far, count); on "]" pop and stitch: previous + inner × count.
decode-string.real: Template expansion and nested config rendering.

random-pick-index.br: Return a random index among those equal to target.
random-pick-index.bt: O(n) time + O(n) memory per pick
random-pick-index.trick: Reservoir sampling: the k-th match replaces the current pick with probability 1/k. Every match ends up equally likely, with O(1) memory.
random-pick-index.real: Sampling from a stream of unknown length: log sampling, telemetry, mini-batch selection.

lfu-cache.br: Evict the least frequently used key (ties → least recently used) in O(1).
lfu-cache.trick: Group keys by use-count, each group in LRU order, and always remember the smallest count. Evict from that group’s front.
lfu-cache.real: Hot-key caches where popularity matters more than recency (CDNs, model-serving feature stores).

random-pick-with-weight.br: Pick index i with probability w[i] / sum(w).
random-pick-with-weight.trick: Lay the weights end to end on a number line. A uniform random point lands in index i’s segment with probability w[i]/total, find the segment with binary search.
random-pick-with-weight.real: Weighted sampling: sampling tokens from a distribution (temperature/top-p), load balancing, reservoir mixes.

subarray-sum-equals-k.br: Count the contiguous subarrays whose sum equals k.
subarray-sum-equals-k.trick: "Subarray sum = k" → prefix[j] − prefix[i] = k, i.e. look up prefix − k. It's Two Sum on running totals.
subarray-sum-equals-k.real: Windowed aggregates over time series; anomaly detection on cumulative metrics.

task-scheduler.pat: Most Frequent Task Sets the Frame
task-scheduler.br: Minimum time to run all tasks with a cooldown n between identical ones.
task-scheduler.trick: "Cooldown scheduling" → lay out the most frequent task as columns of width n+1; everything else just fills the gaps. Answer = max(len(tasks), frame formula).
task-scheduler.real: Batching and rate-limited job scheduling (API calls with per-key cooldowns).

design-circular-queue.br: A fixed-capacity queue where space is reused as items leave.
design-circular-queue.trick: Never move data. Keep a head index and a count; the tail is (head + count) % capacity, so indexes wrap around.
design-circular-queue.real: Ring buffers: network packet queues, audio streams, logging, producer/consumer pipes.

redundant-connection.br: A tree got one extra edge. Return the edge that can be removed.
redundant-connection.trick: "Does this edge make a loop?" → union-find: if both ends already share a root, it does.
redundant-connection.real: Detecting redundant links in networks and merging equivalent entities.

binary-search.br: Find the index of target in a sorted array, or -1.
binary-search.trick: "Sorted + find" → ask the middle one question, throw half the array away. lo/hi/mid, and always move past mid (±1).
binary-search.real: git bisect, searching sorted indexes, and tuning a threshold by halving.

design-hashmap.br: Build put/get/remove without a built-in hash table.
design-hashmap.trick: hash(key) % buckets picks a bucket; collisions chain inside it. Keep the bucket count prime and the chains stay short.
design-hashmap.real: This is literally how dict / HashMap / Redis hash tables work.

accounts-merge.br: Merge accounts that share at least one email.
accounts-merge.trick: "Merge records that share a key" → treat each shared key as a union. One union-find over the emails, then group by root.
accounts-merge.real: Entity resolution: collapsing duplicate customer profiles in a CRM or feature store.

flood-fill.br: Repaint the connected region of the starting pixel with a new colour.
flood-fill.trick: Spread from the start to 4-neighbours that still have the old colour. Painting immediately is your visited marker. Guard: new colour == old colour.
flood-fill.real: The paint-bucket tool, image segmentation, connected-component labelling.

daily-temperatures.br: For each day, how many days until a warmer one?
daily-temperatures.trick: "Next greater element" → stack of unresolved items; a bigger newcomer resolves everything smaller on top of it.
daily-temperatures.real: Next-event lookups: when does a metric next exceed a threshold?

network-delay-time.br: Time for a signal from node k to reach every node (or -1).
network-delay-time.trick: "Shortest path, non-negative weights" → a min-heap of (distance, node). The first time a node pops, its distance is final.
network-delay-time.real: Routing, latency estimation and cheapest-path search over service graphs.

cheapest-flights-within-k-stops.br: Cheapest price from src to dst using at most k stops.
cheapest-flights-within-k-stops.trick: "At most k hops" → Bellman-Ford: do exactly k+1 rounds of relaxing all edges, reading from last round's prices.
cheapest-flights-within-k-stops.real: Budgeted path planning: cheapest route with a cap on hops or retries.

koko-eating-bananas.br: Smallest eating speed that finishes all piles within h hours.
koko-eating-bananas.trick: "Minimum X such that feasible" → feasibility is monotonic, so binary search X directly and test it with a greedy check.
koko-eating-bananas.real: Finding the smallest batch size / throughput that meets a latency budget.

maximum-frequency-stack.br: pop() removes the most frequent element (ties → the most recently pushed).
maximum-frequency-stack.trick: A value pushed for the 3rd time lives on level 3 (and still on levels 1 and 2). Pop from the top level, recency is automatic because each level is a stack.
maximum-frequency-stack.real: Priority by popularity then recency: hot-item eviction, trending queues.

number-of-recent-calls.br: ping(t) returns how many pings happened in [t − 3000, t].
number-of-recent-calls.trick: Pings arrive in increasing time, so expired ones are always at the front: pop them, count what is left.
number-of-recent-calls.real: Sliding-window rate limiting and recent-activity counters.

k-closest-points-to-origin.trick: "Nearest k" → keep a heap of size k whose root is the WORST of the winners; a better candidate evicts it. Think k-NN.

time-based-key-value-store.br: set(key, value, ts) and get(key, ts) → the value with the largest timestamp ≤ ts.
time-based-key-value-store.trick: Timestamps only ever grow, so each key’s list is already sorted → binary-search for "last one ≤ query".
time-based-key-value-store.real: Point-in-time reads in versioned stores, feature stores and time-series DBs ("as of" queries).

longest-common-subsequence.br: Length of the longest subsequence shared by two strings.
longest-common-subsequence.trick: Match → diagonal + 1. No match → best of dropping a char from either string (up or left).
longest-common-subsequence.real: The engine behind diff, git merge, DNA alignment and fuzzy text matching.

snapshot-array.br: An array with snap() and get(index, snap_id).
snapshot-array.trick: Don’t copy the array. Per cell, record (snap_id, value) only when it changes, then binary-search the history.
snapshot-array.real: Version control and MVCC databases: cheap snapshots through copy-on-write.

search-suggestions-system.br: After each typed letter, suggest up to 3 products with that prefix (alphabetical).
search-suggestions-system.trick: "Typeahead" → sort once; matches for a prefix are a contiguous block starting at bisect_left(prefix).
search-suggestions-system.real: Search-box autocomplete and prefix lookups in sorted indexes.

design-browser-history.br: visit / back / forward over a tab’s history.
design-browser-history.trick: History is an array and a cursor. visit() writes at cursor+1 and moves the end marker; back/forward only move the cursor within [0, end).
design-browser-history.real: Undo/redo stacks in editors; navigation stacks in mobile apps.

min-cost-to-connect-all-points.t: Min Cost to Connect All Points
min-cost-to-connect-all-points.br: Connect all points with minimum total Manhattan distance.
min-cost-to-connect-all-points.trick: "Connect everything cheaply" → grow a tree: always add the cheapest edge leaving it (Prim). On dense graphs use plain arrays, no heap.
min-cost-to-connect-all-points.real: Clustering (single-linkage), network design and hierarchical agglomeration.

cache-with-time-limit.br: A key-value cache whose entries expire after a duration.
cache-with-time-limit.trick: Give each entry its own timer that deletes it. Re-setting a key cancels the old timer first. Then count() is just the Map size.
cache-with-time-limit.real: Session caches, OTP/token expiry, TTL caches in front of slow APIs.

memoize.br: Return a function that caches results per distinct argument list.
memoize.trick: Turn the arguments into a lookup path. Same path → return the stored answer instead of calling fn again.
memoize.real: React useMemo/useCallback, selector libraries, caching pure computations.

flatten-deeply-nested-array.br: Flatten an array up to depth n.
flatten-deeply-nested-array.trick: Carry a depth budget. Arrays are opened only while depth > 0; every leaf is pushed into a single output array.
flatten-deeply-nested-array.real: Normalising nested API payloads, menus and tree-like JSON for rendering.

debounce.br: Delay a function until calls stop for t ms.
debounce.trick: One timer in a closure. Each call clears it and starts a new one, only the quiet gap after the LAST call lets it fire.
debounce.real: Search-as-you-type, window resize handlers, autosave, validating form fields.

function-composition.trick: Composition reads right to left. reduceRight does that for you and the empty list naturally returns x.
function-composition.real: Middleware chains, Redux enhancers, data-transformation pipelines.

group-by.trick: One pass: compute the key once, make the bucket if missing (??=), push.
group-by.real: Grouping rows for tables, charts and sectioned lists (also now built in as Object.groupBy).

curry.br: curry(fn) lets you call with arguments split across calls: f(1)(2)(3) = f(1,2,3).
curry.trick: fn.length tells you how many parameters it needs. Keep collecting arguments; once you have enough, call fn.
curry.real: Functional pipelines, event handlers with pre-filled arguments, Redux middleware.

promise-pool.br: Run async functions with at most n running at once.
promise-pool.trick: Start n workers. Each loops: take the next task, await it, repeat. A fast worker is never stuck waiting for a slow one.
promise-pool.real: Rate-limited uploads, crawlers, parallel API calls with a concurrency cap, test runners.

promise-time-limit.br: Wrap an async function so it rejects with "Time Limit Exceeded" if it takes longer than t ms.
promise-time-limit.trick: Promise.race between the real call and a timer that rejects. Clear the timer in finally.
promise-time-limit.real: API timeouts, fetch with AbortController, circuit breakers and health checks.

throttle.br: Run fn at most once per t ms: first call immediately, then the latest queued call when the window ends.
throttle.trick: Run the first call now, open a t ms window. Calls inside it just overwrite "pending". When the window ends, run the pending one and open a new window.
throttle.real: Scroll/mousemove handlers, rate-limited API calls, analytics batching.

chunk-array.br: Split an array into subarrays of length size (the last may be shorter).
chunk-array.trick: Step i by size and slice(i, i + size). slice is safe past the end, so the short last chunk needs no special case.
chunk-array.real: Pagination, batching API requests, splitting work across workers.

event-emitter.br: subscribe(event, cb) returns {unsubscribe}; emit(event, args) calls every callback and returns their results.
event-emitter.trick: Per event keep a set of subscriptions. Wrap each callback in its own object so unsubscribing removes exactly that subscription, even for duplicates.
event-emitter.real: DOM events, Node EventEmitter, Redux/store subscriptions, message buses.

join-two-arrays-by-id.br: Merge two arrays of objects on id; arr2 wins on conflicts; result sorted by id.
join-two-arrays-by-id.trick: Key everything by id in a Map, spread-merge (later object wins), then sort by id once.
join-two-arrays-by-id.real: Joining API responses, merging user profiles, left/right-join logic in front-end data layers.

sort-by.br: Sort an array ascending by the value returned from fn(item).
sort-by.trick: If computing the key is costly, compute it once per item, sort the (key, item) pairs, then drop the keys (Schwartzian transform).
sort-by.real: Sorting by an expensive derived value: relevance scores, parsed dates, distance to a point.
